methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Lab 91 is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for robust median pricing.

Of three triangulation methods tested, only Stage-Progression was applicable. This method uses the $10M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression in the sector, yielding a $25M implied valuation. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be executed because Lab 91's revenue is not on file—a common constraint for private companies. Peer-Median analysis was rejected as inapplicable: while 13 same-sector peers exist, filtering by stage, timing, or valuation tier yielded fewer than 3 datapoints, making any single-method median unreliable and vulnerable to outlier distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with $25M as the median point. This range reflects stage-typical progression mathematics but carries material uncertainty. Key limitations include reliance on a single applicable method, absence of revenue data to cross-check against public sector multiples (18.9x median P/S), and an insufficient private peer cohort for independent validation. Resolution of the revenue figure and identification of closer-stage private comparables would strengthen conviction.
